text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Swedish Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance has abandoned a donor initiative at brokering inter-party talks to resolve the country's political impasse.
- Mines Minister Christon Tembo says the Binani Group will set up an acid plant at the newly privatised Luanshya and Baluba mines.
- Amnesty International lists Zambia among 14 African countries which passed the death sentence last year.
- President Frederick Chiluba has urged members of parliament to take the lead in developing a home-grown democracy as opposed to the kind dictated to the country by external forces.
- The law association has urged the government to come up with a code of conduct for members of the judiciary to guide them in their work.
- The government has threatened to arrest former president Kennth Kaunda for burning voters cards surrendered to him by his supporters.
